EW03_Joseph__v1.note: The 'I am Joseph' reveal (Gen 45) was on the SECOND visit with all eleven brothers present (Benjamin included); 'ten' belongs to the first visit. Dropped the false count.
EW03_Joseph__v1.before: But on that day, ten travel-worn men came begging me for grain, not knowing the ruler they bowed to. They were my brothers — the very brothers who had sold me, whose faces I had carried in the dark for half my life.
EW03_Joseph__v1.after: But on that day, my travel-worn brothers came begging me for grain, not knowing the ruler they bowed to — the very brothers who had sold me, whose faces I had carried in the dark for half my life.

EW01_Two_Goats__v1__short.note: Lev 16:21 has the scapegoat sent away 'by the hand of a fit man' — the high priest did not personally drive it out. Same Aaron-overclaim family as the prior Lev 10 catch.
EW01_Two_Goats__v1__short.before: confessed every sin of the people over it, and drove it into the desert to be lost.
EW01_Two_Goats__v1__short.after: confessed every sin of the people over it, and sent it away into the desert to be lost.

02_Psalm_22_Song_From_The_Cross__v1__sho.note: 'did not speak His own words first' implies the dereliction cry was Jesus' opening word from the cross; Luke 23:34 ('Father, forgive them') precedes it. Reworded to keep the hook (borrowed words) without the false order. All 4 panel reviewers confirmed. Re-verify panel then flagged that 'not His own' undercuts inspiration (1 Pet 1:11 — Spirit of Christ in the prophets) and fought 'made it His own'; refined to the neutral 'reached for words already written' hook.
02_Psalm_22_Song_From_The_Cross__v1__sho.before: From the cross, Jesus did not speak His own words first — He cried a psalm David had written a thousand years before.
02_Psalm_22_Song_From_The_Cross__v1__sho.after: From the cross, in His darkest hour, Jesus reached for words already written — a psalm David had penned a thousand years before.
